title: England's beavers turned dense Dorset woodland into wetland in just one year
content: Beavers newly introduced in Dorset have remarkably transformed a woodland area into a flourishing wetland. Through their natural dam-building, these creatures have slowed down water movement, resulting in the formation of deep pools. This ecological shift has rejuvenated the local fauna, reintroducing various native species to the Purbeck region. Additionally, the beaver dams serve to mitigate flooding on nearby roads during heavy rains, highlighting nature’s essential contribution to environmental resilience.

title: Anne LaBastille's off-grid Adirondack home and 32 acres are now protected

Her life there was immortalized in her famous 'Woodswoman' memoir series, capturing the essence of nature. Later, her beloved property was turned over to New York State for conservation, now part of the Forest Preserve, showcasing her lasting impact in inspiring nature lovers and protecting the great outdoors.

title: How WhatsApp messages led to former USCIS official in $960,000 citizenship scam

Investigators used thousands of WhatsApp messages and calls to trace the alleged scam. The scheme involved bypassing standard procedures and speeding up citizenship cases. This alleged operation spanned over six years, from late 2019 to early 2026.

Boeing and Northrop Grumman are competing for this significant contract, which could be worth billions. This advanced aircraft is intended to replace the aging F/A-18 Super Hornet fleet. The new fighter is expected to enter service in the 2030s and will feature advanced stealth.

title: 5.3-magnitude quake hits Tibet as region reels from deadly flash floods
content: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake struck Tibet recently, following another tremor last week.  Devastating flash floods hit the Tibet-Nepal border on August 26, causing widespread destruction.  The disaster has raised concerns over the fragile Qinghai-Tibet Plateau environment.  Rising temperatures and glacier melt are cited as contributing factors to the floods.  Nepal's death toll from the floods has risen to 1,357 people.

title: Ballon d’Or shortlist: Dembélé, Mbappé, Kane, Messi, Yamal lead star-studded race

Meanwhile, the women's award faces a shift in dynamics following Aitana Bonmatí's absence. The winners will be announced during a glamorous ceremony in London on October 26.

title: T20 leagues taking over? Ponting fears ODI cricket will be 'played less'
content: Ricky Ponting expresses concern over the potential decline of ODI cricket as T20 leagues gain popularity worldwide. He views this shift as an unavoidable part of the sport's evolution, which leaves him disheartened about the future of 50-over matches. Despite this, Ponting remains optimistic that Test cricket will thrive, as major cricketing nations continue to value the longest format.

title: Flipkart widens lead against Amazon as quick commerce surges
content: Flipkart is growing its user base faster than Amazon in India.  This expands its lead in online retail significantly over recent years.  Flipkart's quick-commerce business, Flipkart Minutes, is also scaling up rapidly.  It is now handling millions of orders daily, nearing established rivals.  The company's user base growth contrasts with Amazon's contracting numbers.

title: Hong Kong or Singapore: Which country should expats choose in 2026?
content: Hong Kong and Singapore compete as Asia's top financial hubs, offering expat opportunities.  Singapore provides a more spacious and structured environment for residents.  Hong Kong offers a faster-paced, denser urban experience with strong China connections.  Career opportunities vary, with Hong Kong strong in finance and Singapore in tech.  Both cities attract wealthy foreigners for housing, wealth management, and luxury sales.

Following recent losses, seven players were axed, and the coaching staff saw modifications as well. title: Does AfD's big win in Germany signal a 'far right' uprising in Europe?
content: Many years ago, Otto von Bismarck observed that politics was “the art of the possible”. The modern European establishment appears to have inverted the Iron Chancellor’s maxim. Politics has increasingly become the art of explaining to voters why what they want is impossible, irresponsible, xenophobic, Islamophobic, nativist or, inevitably, far right. And made it impossible to vote for the so-called far-right party that’s actually willing to admit there’s a problem.

title: UAE leader had warned Netanyahu of Hamas attack days before Oct 7 massacre: Report
content: sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed reportedly delivered prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu a direct warning of a major attack . title: Trump takes trade war with Canada to ice
content: ties hit the ice after Trump threatened to shut Canadian aircraft maker bombardier out of the american market unless it moves production to the US and Ottawa began imposing retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion of U.S. goods . the sharp escalation in a trade war between two countries that once pride themselves on having the world's least dramatic border wasaccompanied by bizarre theatrics from Washington .

title: BJP demands Punjab CM's resignation over farmer's suicide
content: BJP demands the resignation of CM Bhagwant Mann after a man died by suicide . BJP played a video of the man who consumed pesticide, narrating the incident . the man named those who allegedly threatened him, a BJP spokesperson says .

title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta dies by suicide at Noida residence
content: mehta, 74, a 1975-batch IAS officer, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at his Sector 82 residence on September 6 . he cited his "mental and health issues" as the reasons behind the extreme step . his body was cremated at the Lodhi Road crematorium .

title: Iran launched fresh attack on US navy ships Monday amid China, Russia aid fears
content: the reported attack came after Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer over the weekend . the repeated attempts to target american warships have raised concerns that Iran may be using more advanced weapons and could be receiving help from China or Russia .

title: Ladakh LG taps 90 million litres of glacial water after village head's appeal
content: nearly 90 million litres of glacial water have started irrigating 12 villages in ladakh every day . the massive volume of glacier-melt, previously flowing untapped into the River Indus, is now being channelised into the Igoo-Phey Irrigation Canal . it was an appeal from a village chief that drove the LG to brainstorm on harnessing glaciers and snowmelt for productive use .

title: Over 600 flights cancelled as air traffic control glitch disrupts UK airports
content: more than 600 flights were canceled, according to flightradar24 . the issue was linked to its flight processing system . engineers were working to restore normal operations after the problem affected airports across the country . at least 625 flights arriving at or departing from UK airports had been cancelled .

title: US targets Iran’s entire aviation sector with fresh sanctions
content: the sanctions target "36 targets for supporting Iran's aviation sector," a treasury official says . the measures cover 27 Iranian airlines and companies based in countries including the united arab emirates, Turkey, Malaysia and Kazakhstan . sanctions come as the US and Iran remain locked in a war that began in late February .

title: NIA drops UAPA against American, 6 Ukrainians held in 'terror link' case
content: the chargesheet invokes sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 . the accused had valid travel documents but didn't obtain the mandatory Protected Area Permit (PAP) required to enter Mizoram . NIA said its probe into the UAPA aspect remains underway .

title: Ahead of Brics, India & China hold military talks in Arunachal
content: the first-ever Corps Commander–level meeting between india and china in the eastern sector was a two-day engagement . the meeting marked a milestone in bilateral efforts to maintain peace along the line of actual control (LAC) ties between the two nations are gradually improving .
